1.say: You marked this sentence. 'They introduced the rule in May and complaints fell.' It is clear, but it is a story. A report wants a claim you can measure. 'The introduction of the rule in May led to a fall in complaints.' Better. Now the reader can ask how big the fall was. It feels heavier. It is heavier. Use it for the claims, not for every line, or nobody finishes the page. And the long phrase you crossed out? 'The recent decision by the committee to delay the report published last week.' Too many joins. 'The committee's recent decision to delay the report.' Now the reader knows whose decision it was without reading it twice. So the rule is: pack it, but not until it breaks. Write that on the wall.

grammar.label: nominalisation — turning a verb into a noun phrase
grammar.form: verb + -tion / -ment / -al / -ure / -ance, used as the subject or object
grammar.meaning: packages an action as a thing so that it can be measured, caused or compared

explanation.en: 'They introduced the rule in May, and complaints fell' becomes 'The introduction of the rule in May led to a fall in complaints.' Nominalisation makes writing dense and impersonal — useful in a report, heavy everywhere else.

grammar.negative_example: The close of the factory caused considerable hardship.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbek tilida harakat nomi '-ish' bilan muntazam yasaladi; ingliz tilida esa qo'shimcha har bir fe'l uchun alohida yodlanadi.

grammar.label: complex noun phrases — stacking modifiers
grammar.form: determiner + adjective(s) + noun + prepositional phrase / relative clause / participle
grammar.meaning: one long phrase carries what would otherwise need several sentences

explanation.en: English piles information after the noun as well as before it: 'the recent decision by the committee to delay the report published last week'. Order matters — adjectives before, phrases and clauses after, closest modifier nearest the noun.
explanation.uz: Ingliz tilida ma'lumot otdan oldin ham, keyin ham joylashadi: sifatlar oldin, ibora va ergash gaplar keyin. Otga eng yaqin aniqlovchi unga eng tegishlisi bo'ladi.

grammar.positive_example: The committee's recent decision to delay the report surprised nobody.
grammar.negative_example: The recent committee's decision for delaying the report surprised nobody.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbek tilida barcha aniqlovchilar otdan oldin keladi; ingliz tilida ibora va ergash gaplar otdan keyin turadi — bu tartib alohida mashq talab qiladi.
